Hi Sara — Stephanie from Redwood Legal. Thanks for initiating. Quick answers and our proposed positions so your team can decide whether to redline: 

- Transfers: Redwood proposes SCCs (we keep them updated to the latest EC decision). For added assurance we include standard encryption, access controls, and audit logging in the DPA. If Nimbus requires BCRs as a mandatory baseline, please confirm the reason — BCRs are an enterprise-level commitment and require longer lead time.

- Subprocessors: we maintain a published allowlist and provide 30 days' notice for new subprocessors. If Nimbus needs an explicit approval right or additional vetting, we can discuss a limited safelisting carve-out (e.g., for security-sensitive subprocessors).

- eSign: Redwood issues via DocuSign envelopes by default. We can route to AdobeSign at the customer's request; however, certain enterprise procurement systems require DocuSign integration. We have a standard workflow: legal uploads finalized DPA, sales triggers DocuSign envelope, Procurement signs, then exec counter-signs.

Suggested next steps for speed: 1) Nimbus to send any procurement intake form if required; 2) Nimbus to confirm whether SCCs + contractual safeguards are sufficient; 3) If so, we will accept limited Nimbus redlines to the DPA and circulate a DocuSign envelope for signature.

I attached a short redlines_summary.docx with the clauses we expect to hold firm vs. those we can be flexible on. Happy to join a 20–30m call if helpful.

Thanks,
